description_en: Mhāsukhvāḥmāju Dyaḥchẽ is the god-house of Vajrayoginī situated northwest of the deity’s main temple in Sankhu.Mhāsukhvāḥmāju (lit. goddess with yellow face) is a vernacular name of Vajrayoginī. The statue of Vajrayoginī is yellow in color, as it is plated with gold. Therefore, she is locally known as Mhāsukhvāḥmāju. As the statue of Vajrayoginī inside the sanctum of her main temple is enshrined permanently, a replica of her was made for the annual procession. The Dyaḥchẽ is the God House where the replica, widely referred to as Mhāsukhvāḥmāju, is enshrined. The two-story Dyaḥchẽ facing north has copper sheets laid on the roof with three goldenkalaśas installed as its finial. The sanctum of the Dyaḥchẽ is on the first floor where the statue of Mhāsukhvāḥmāju is enshrined at the center facing west. She is three-eyed carrying a blue lotus with her left hand and akhaḍgawith the right. Usually, deities are seen holding akhaḍgawith their palm. However, Mhāsukhvāḥmāju does not hold thekhaḍga, but the emblem is tied to her fingers with a piece of cloth. She originally carried avajrawith her right palm. After she defeated Śaṅkarācārya, a renowned ascetic and philosopher of the 8th century, in a doctrinal debate, she inhumed her vajra in her womb and held akhaḍga. Since then, she also came to be known as Khaḍgayoginī. It is unclear what her statue is made of, as the whole figure is always covered with shiny clothes. According to a Vajrācārya, the inner body of the deity is made of wood covered with gilded copper (B. Shrestha2012, p. 406). Statues of Siṃhinī, the lion-faced deity, and Vasundharā are enshrined to her right in the north and Vyāghrinī, the tiger-faced deity, and Vasundhara to her left in the south. Both Siṃhinī and Vyāghrinī are taken around the town on separate palanquins together with Mhāsukhvāḥmāju during the annual procession. Effigies of Maitreya and Lokeśvara are established in the southern corner of the sanctum. Locals, however, refer to Maitreya as Kau Mahārānī (lit. blacksmith queen) (B. Shrestha2012, p. 407;M. Slusser1972, p. 22). The figure of Maitreya is believed to date back to the 9th century while the Lokeśvara statue is believed to belong to the 13th-14th century (M. Slusser1972, p. 22-23). The Dyaḥchẽ also serves as the residence of the priest of Jogeśvara Mandira (SKH0510).A south-facingmĩgāḥ(lit. fire pit;agnimaṭha) is established to the west of the entrance. Fire always burns in this Agnimaṭha. It is believed that putting asinhaḥof the ashes of the Agnimaṭha protects a person from witches and evil spirits. A room on the eastern side of the ground floor has a Svayambhū Caitya established at the center. The Caitya made of gilt copper is a replica of the Svayambhū Caitya in Jogeśvara Mandira. The Caitya at the Dyaḥchẽ’s ground floor is also taken around the town during the annual procession of Mhāsukhvāḥmāju. A head-figure of the Buddha and an overturnedkarāhī(a thick circular pot mostly used for shallow or deep frying) are placed north of the Svayambhū Caitya. Locals identify the Head-figure of the Buddha as the head of King Vikramāditya and connect the Karāhī to a legend related to the King. According to the legend, Nepalese King Dharmāgata, who ruled from Viśālanagara, used to cook his body in the boiling oil on the Karāhī and feed Vajrayoginī at night. Pleased with his offering, the Goddess would bring the King back to life. Vikramāditya, the King of Ujjayana, came to stay at the King’s palace as a servant and began spying on him. One day, he saw the King cooking himself in oil and feeding his flesh to the Goddess. The next night, Vikramāditya went early and fed himself to the Goddess in the same manner but only after applying spices all over his body. The Goddess was left sated and content by the taste of Vikramāditya’s flesh and granted him a large amount of wealth. Later, when Dharmāgata came for the offering, the Goddess instructed the King to overturn the Karāhī, saying that she was already sated (N. Pauḍela2020, p. 61-62). Another legend associated with the Head-figure relates it to Prince Mānadeva’s unintentional beheading of his father King Vikamānti. Later, when Mānadeva finds out that he has decapitated his father, he laments his action and takes refuge in Maṇiyoginī (Vajrayoginī), which causes the head of Vikamānti to attain a divine perfection in the vicinity of the Goddess (Nepālikabhūpavaṃśāvali6.52-58).According to a Buddhist scripture calledMaṇiśailaMahāvadāna, Jogadeva Vajrācārya organized a procession of Vajrayoginī together with a goldencaityaand statues of Siṃhinī and Vyāghrinī in 1317 BC (Kaligata Era 1818) as per the instruction of Vajrayoginī (V. VajrācāryaNS 1119, p. 34). Besides this reference, there is no other historic source that records the first installation of these statues inside the Dyaḥchẽ. One of the medieval annals refers to this Dyaḥchẽ as Mura Capāra (T. Siṃha1136, 3-4, folio 3A-4A) and Thaone Capāra (T. Siṃha1136, 20, folio 33A). This infers that the Dyaḥchẽ was only acapāḥduring the medieval period. It was renovated in 1693 CE (NS 813) (P. Śreṣṭha and P. Kāfle2077, p. 91). In 1751 CE (NS 871), the western of the three finials of the Dyaḥchẽ fell off. The king was informed and special rituals for auspiciousness were performed (T. Siṃha1136, p. 22, folio 35A). In an unfortunate event in 1915 CE (VS 1971), the Agnimaṭha at the Dyaḥchẽ caused a massive fire that gutted down all the statues in the building except the Head-figure of the Buddha and the Karāhī. All the statues at the Dyaḥchẽ were then shifted to the Caugharā Sataḥ (SKH0560). Prime minister Candra Śamśera had disbursed necessary funds for reinstating the damaged statues and performing consecration rituals (P. SakvaVS 2074, p. 45-47;Devamālāvaṃśāvalī, p. 18). The 2015 earthquakes caused damages to the Dyaḥchẽ and was reconstructed. After the completion of the reconstruction in 2017 CE, all the statues including the image of Mhāsukhvāḥmāju were then brought back to the Dyaḥchẽ.There are more records related to the statues at the Dyaḥchẽ in other annals. During the reign of King Śivasiṃha Malla in 1597 CE (NS 717), Amṛtarāja Bhāro of Sankhu sponsored the renovation of Mhāsukhvāḥmāju’s statue (Vajrācārya et alnd). The Statue was again renovated and gilded during the reign of King Lakṣmīnarasiṃha Malla in 1625 CE (NS 745) (T. Siṃha1136, p. 16, folio 24B). in 1750 CE (NS 870), the statue of Vyāghrinī in the Dyaḥchẽ caught fire at its chest. The incident was reported to the king and special rituals for auspiciousness were performed (T. Siṃha1136, p. 20, folio 33A).The priest of Jogeśvara Mandira performs the daily worship of the deities enshrined at the Dyaḥchẽ as well. The priest has to reside in the Dyaḥchẽ along with his family for a week. Every year, Vajrayoginī Jātrā is observed for eight days in Sankhu beginning from the full moon day of Caitra. On the 3rd of the dark fortnight of Vaiśākha, the fourth day, a procession of the statues of Mhāsukhvāḥmāju, Siṃhinī, Vyāghrinī, Svayambhū Caitya, and Vasundharā takes place. On the 8th of the dark fortnight of Vaiśākha, the statues are brought back to the Dyaḥchẽ marking the end of the Jātrā.
description_ne: म्हासुख्वा:माजु द्य:छेँ वज्रयोगिनी देवीको द्य:छेँ हो जहाँ उनको जात्रा गरिने मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ ।यस द्य:छेँ वज्रयोगिनी मन्दिरभन्दा माथि उत्तर-पश्चिममा रहेको छ । जोगेश्वर मन्दिर(SKH0510) मा पूजा गर्ने पूजारी पनि यसै द्यःछेँमा बस्छन् । म्हासुख्वाःमाजु भनेका वज्रयोगिनी नै हुन् । वज्रयोगिनीको मन्दिरभित्र रहेको वज्रयोगिनीको मूल मूर्ति निकाल्न नमिल्ने हुनाले जात्रा गर्नको लागि प्रतिकृति स्वरूप उक्त मूर्ति बनाइएको हो । मूर्तिको अनुहारमा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएकोले पहेँलो देखिन्छ र पहेँलो अनुहार हुनाले वज्रयोगिनीको यस मूर्तिलाई म्हासुख्वाःमाजु भनिएको हो । उत्तराभिमुख गरी बनाइएको यो द्यःछेँ दुई तलाको छ । द्यःछेँमा तामाको छाना राखी तीनवटा सुवर्ण गजूर राखिएका छन् । द्यःछेँको पहिलो तलामा म्हासुख्वाःमाजुको गर्भगृह रहेको छ । गर्भगृहको मध्य भागमा पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी म्हासुख्वाःमाजुको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । देवीका तीनवटा आँखा छन् र अनुहारमा सुनको जलप लगाइएको छ । उनको दायाँ हातमा खड्ग रहेको छ । सामान्यतया देवीदेवताहरूले खड्ग समातेका हुन्छन्, तर यहाँ म्हासुख्वाःमाजुले खड्ग समातेका छैनन्, कपडाले देवीको औंलामा खड्ग बाँधिएको छ । पहिले उनले दायाँ हातमा वज्र धारण गरेका थिए, पछि शङ्कराचार्यलाई शास्त्रार्थमा पराजित गरेपछि आफ्नो वज्रलाई गर्भमा राखी खड्ग धारण गरेका थिए । त्यस बेलादेखि उनलाई खड्गयोगिनी पनि भन्न थालिएको हो । उनले बायाँ हातले नीलउत्पल समातेका छन् । देवीको सम्पूर्ण शरीर कपडाले ढाकेकोले कुन वस्तुले शरीर बनेको भन्ने कुरा देखिँदैन । एकजना वज्राचार्यका अनुसार शरीरको भित्र काठ राखी बाहिर सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको तामाको पाताले छोपिएको हो (B. Shrestha2012, p. 406) । उनको दायाँ (उत्तरमा) सिंहिनी र वसुन्धरा स्थापना गरिएका छन् । त्यस्तै बायाँ (दक्षिणमा) व्याघ्रिनी र वसुन्धरा स्थापना गरिएका छन् । सिंहिनी र व्याघ्रिनीलाई पनि म्हासुख्वाःमाजु सँगै खटमा राखेर जात्रा गरिन्छ । गर्भगृहको दक्षिणपट्टि कुनामा मैत्रेय बुद्ध र लोकेश्वर स्थापना गरिएका छन् । मैत्रेय बुद्धलाई स्थानीयहरू कौ महारानी (blacksmith queen) भन्ने गर्छन् (B. Shrestha2012, p. 407;M. Slusser1972, p. 22) । मैत्रेय बुद्धलाई नवौं शताब्दी र लोकेश्वरलाई १३-१४ औं शताब्दीको मानिन्छ (M. Slusser1972, p. 22-23) ।द्यःछेँको भुइँतलामा प्रवेशद्वारको पश्चिमपट्टि दक्षिणाभिमुख गरीमिगाः(अग्निमठ) बनाइएको छ । त्यस अग्निमठमा सधैं आगो बलिरहन्छ । त्यहाँको खरानीको टीका लगाएपछि बोक्सी वा अन्य दुष्ट आत्माहरूले छुन सक्दैन भन्ने विश्वास गरिन्छ ।  भुइँतलाको पूर्वपट्टि कोठा बनाइएको छ । त्यस कोठाको मध्यभागमा स्वयम्भू चैत्य स्थापना गरिएको छ । जोगेश्वर मन्दिरभित्रको स्वयम्भू चैत्यको प्रतिकृति स्वरूप उक्त चैत्य बनाइएको हो । तामाको चैत्यमा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको छ । म्हासुख्वाःमाजुको जात्रामा उक्त स्वयम्भू चैत्यलाई पनि खटमा राखेर नगर परिक्रमा गराइन्छ । स्वयम्भू चैत्यको उत्तरमा तामाबाट निर्मित बुद्धको शिर र दक्षिणमा घोप्ट्याइएको कराही राखिएको छ । स्थानीयहरू बुद्धको शिरलाई राजा विक्रमादित्यको शिर मान्छन् र कराहीलाई पनि विक्रमादित्यको कथासँग जोडेर व्याख्या गर्छन् । नेपालमा राजा धर्मागतले दिनदिनै कराहीमा तेल तताएर आफ्नो शरीरलाई तेलमा पकाएर देवीलाई खुवाउँथे । देवी खुसी भई उनलाई पुनः जीवनदान दिन्थिन् । उज्जयनका राज विक्रमादित्यले धर्मागत राजाको सेवक भई चियोचर्चा गर्न थाले । राजाले आफू स्वयंलाई तेलमा पकाएर देवीलाई खुवाएको दृष्य देखे । भोलिपल्ट धर्मागत आउनुभन्दा अघि नै विक्रमादित्यले आफ्नो शरीरमा मसला लेपन गरी कराहीमा तेल तताएर आफ्नो शरीरलाई तेलमा पकाएर देवीलाई खुवाए । देवीलाई पहिलेको भन्दा विक्रमादित्यको पकवान मीठो लाग्यो र उनलाई धेरै धनसम्पत्ति दिए । केही बेरपछि धर्मागत आएर आफूलाई पकाएर खुवाउनु खोज्दा देवीले अब तिमीले पकवान बनाउनु पर्दैन, यो कराही घोप्ट्याइदेऊ भनिन् (N. Pauḍela2020, p. 61-62) । अर्को एक कथानुसार मानदेवले अज्ञानवश आफ्नो बुबा विकमान्तिको शिर छेदन गरी गरी हत्या गरेका थिए । पछि मारिने व्यक्ति आफ्नै बुबा भन्ने थाहा पाएपछि विलाप गरी मणियोगिनी (वज्रयोगिनी) को शरणमा पुगेपछि विकमान्तिको शिर त्यहीँ सिद्ध भएको थियो (Nepālikabhūpavaṃśāvali6.52-58) । यस कथालाई पुष्टि गर्ने कुनै ऐतिहासिक आधार देखिँदैन ।मणिशैल महावदानअनुसार कलिगत सम्वत् १८१८ पौष कृष्ण १० मा जोगदेव वज्राचार्यले वज्रयोगिनीदेवीको आज्ञाअनुसार उग्रतारा वज्रयोगिनी, चैत्य, सिंहिनी, व्याघ्रिनीको सुवर्ण मूर्ति बनाई जात्रा चलाएका थिए (V. Vajrācārya1119, p. 34) । द्यःछेँ र भित्र रहेका मूर्तिहरूको प्रथम निर्माणकालबारे जानकारी दिने ऐतिहासिक प्रमाण पाइँदैन । मध्यकालमा लिखित घटनावलीमा यस द्यःछेँलाईमुर चपार(T. Siṃha1136, 3-4, folio 3A-4A) रथओने चपार(T. Siṃha1136, 20, folio 33A) भनिएको छ । यसबाट अहिले पक्की द्यःछेँ निर्माण गरिएको भएपनि मध्यकालमा यो चपाः मात्रै थियो भन्ने कुरा थाहा पाइन्छ । नेसं ८१३ (सन् १६९३) मा द्यःछेँको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो (P. Śreṣṭha and P. Kāfle2077, p. 91) । नेसं ८७१ (सन् १७५१) मा द्यःछेँको छानामा राखिएका तीनवटा गजूरमध्ये पश्चिमपट्टिको गजूर खसेको थियो । राजालाई खबर गरी शान्तिस्वस्ति गरिएको थियो (T. Siṃha1136, p. 22, folio 35A) । विसं १९७१ (सन् १९१५) मा राजा त्रिभुवन र प्रधानमन्त्री चन्द्रशमशेरको पालामा म्हासुख्वा:माजुको द्य:छेँमा रहेको अग्निमठबाट आगो सल्किएर दीपङ्कर बुद्धको टाउको र घोप्ट्याइएको कराही बाहेक अन्य मूर्तिहरू ध्वस्त भएका थिए । द्य:छेँमा भएका देवदेवीका मूर्तिहरू चौघरा सत: (SKH0560) मा सारिएका थिए । आगलागीबाट ध्वस्त भएका मूर्तिहरू फेरि बनाएर जीवन्यास राखी पूर्ववत् स्थानमा स्थापना गर्नको लागि चन्द्रशमशेरबाट चाहिने खर्च निकासा दिइएको थियो (P. SakvaVS 2074, p. 45-47;Devamālāvaṃśāvalī, p. 18) । विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पले द्यःछेँमा क्षति पुगेकोले पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो । विसं २०७४ (सन् २०१७) मा पुनर्निर्माणको कार्य सम्पन्न भएपछि म्हासुख्वाःमाजु लगायत देवीदेवतालाई द्यःछेँमा सारिएको थियो ।द्यःछेँमा राखिएका मूर्तिबारे पनि घटनावलीहरूमा टिपिएका छन् । नेसं ७१७ (सन् १५९७) मा राजा शिवसिंह मल्लको पालामा साँखुका अमृतराज भारोले म्हासुख्वाःमाजुको मूर्ति जीर्णोद्धार गरेका थिए (Vajrācārya et alnd) । नेसं ७४५ (सन् १६२५) मा राजा लक्ष्मीनरसिंह मल्लको पालामा म्हासुख्वाःमाजुको मूर्ति जीर्ण भएकोले जीर्णोद्धार गरी सुनको जलप लगाइएको थियो (T. Siṃha1136, p. 16, folio 24B) । नेसं ८७० (सन् १७५०) मा द्यःछेँमा राखिएको व्याघ्रिनीको छातीमा आगो लागेकोले राजालाई खबर गरी शान्तिस्वस्ति गरिएको थियो (T. Siṃha1136, p. 20, folio 33A) ।प्रत्येक दिन जोगेश्वर मन्दिरमा नित्यपूजा गर्ने पूजारीले यस द्यःछेँमा रहेका देवीदेवतालाई पनि पूजा गर्छन् । ती पूजारी परिवारसहित एक हप्तासम्म यसै द्यःछेँमा सुत्नुपर्छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष चैत्र शुक्ल पूर्णिमादेखि आठ दिनसम्म वज्रयोगिनीको जात्रा मनाइन्छ । जात्राको चौथो दिन वैशाख कृष्ण ३ मा द्यःछेँमा राखिएका म्हासुख्वाःमाजु, सिंहिनी, व्याघ्रिनी, स्वयम्भू चैत्य र वसुन्धरालाई खटमा राखेर जात्रा गरिन्छ । वैशाख कृष्ण ८ मा देवतालाई पुनः द्यःछेँमा ल्याएर विधिपूर्वक स्थापना गरिन्छ ।

historical_events.event_description: Mhāsukhvāḥmāju was dismounted from her seat at the Dyaḥchẽ and brought to the town of Sankhu. This probably is the earliest historic record of thekhaṭajātrāof Mhāsukhvāḥmāju.

historical_events.event_name: Kathmandu's victory over Bhaktapur with blessings of Mhāsukhvāḥmāju
historical_events.event_description: King Mahendra Malla, the king of Kathmandu, had invaded Bhaktapur and was victorious after offering special worship to Mhāsukhvāḥmāju and having received her blessings.
During the reign of King Śivasiṃha Malla, Amṛtarāja Bhāro of Sankhu sponsored the renovation of Mhāsukhvāḥmāju’s statue.
King Lakṣmīnarasiṃha Malla got the statue of Ekajaṭā (Mhasukhvāḥmāju) renovated and gilded.

historical_events.event_name: Death of King Pratāpa Malla halts Mhāsukhvāḥmāju's procession
historical_events.event_description: King Pratāpa Malla died on the 11th/12th of the bright fortnight of Caitra in 1674 CE (NS 794). The annual procession of Mhāsukhvāḥmāju was not observed that year. It was possibly the only occasion in history when the procession was not taken out.

historical_events.event_name: Palanquin of Svayambhū Caitya lands on the ground
historical_events.event_description: The palanquin of Svayambhū Caitya lands on the ground, as the people carrying it failed to maintain their balance. It was not taken to be a serious incident and no ritual for auspiciousness was performed. Shortly afterward, King Pārthivendra Malla’s mother passed away in 1683 CE (NS 803).
The Mhāsukhvāḥmāju Dyaḥchẽ was renovated. The entry in the annals does not mention the name of the sponsor.
The statue of Vyāghrinī in the Dyaḥchẽ caught fire at its chest. The incident was reported to the king and special rituals for auspiciousness were performed.

historical_events.event_name: Falling of one of the three finials
historical_events.event_description: The western finial of the Dyaḥchẽ fell off. The king was informed and special rituals for auspiciousness were performed.

During the reign of King Tribhuvana and the prime ministership of Candra Śamśera, the Agnimaṭha at the Dyaḥchẽ caused a massive fire that gutted the statues in the building except the head-figure of the Buddha and the Karāhī. All the statues at the Dyaḥchẽ were then shifted to the Caugharā Sataḥ. Candra Śamśera disbursed necessary funds for reinstating the damaged statues and performing consecration rituals.
Although the Dyaḥchẽ did not collapse due to the earthquakes, the jolts left many cracks on the building.

The Department of Archaeology funded and managed the reconstruction of the Dyaḥchẽ. Upon completion, all statues including Mhāsukhvāḥmāju that were stored at Caugharā Sataḥ were brought back to the Mhāsukhvāḥmāju Dyaḥchẽ.

The family of Lieutenant Colonel Indra Bahādura Śāha of Bāhuna Gāũ in Sakuna Maijā of Salyāna offers a bell. As a portion of the inscription is covered by some substance, the full content of the inscription is unclear. But there is a name, Major Iśvarī Bahādura Śāha, inscribed above the main inscription, which is a later addition. Probably, Iśvarī Bahādura Śāha was the main donor and his name was inscribed again after it was covered by the substance in the original inscription.

The content of the three-line inscription does not record an event but only states the year and the name of the reigning king. It is so far the earliest inscription in a vernacular language (Newari) of Nepal. The year is given in words that literally mean ‘an excess of 3 [and] 9 in the era 200’ (Tamoṭa NS 1097, p. 34). When this is read in reverse, it becomes 200-9-3, i.e., 293. Any year given in non-numeral form or numeral words is read in reverse. The inscription only states ‘during the reign of King Rudradeva in the year 293’ (Tamoṭa NS 1097, p. 34). Therefore, the event is unclear. As the inscription is on the pillar, it probably is the record of its erection.
